per_transfer_phases: ADDRESS_PHASE: one HCLK cycle (extended if previous data phase asserts HREADY=LOW). Manager drives HADDR + HBURST + HSIZE + HTRANS + HPROT + HWRITE + HMASTLOCK + (HNONSEC + HEXCL + HMASTER when AHB5) + (HWSTRB defaults if HWRITE=1).

DATA_PHASE: one or more HCLK cycles. Manager drives HWDATA / HWSTRB on writes; Subordinate drives HRDATA / HRESP / HREADYOUT (+ HEXOKAY when Exclusive). Data phase ends on the first rising HCLK with HREADY=HIGH.
ahb_fsm_hints.address_phase_rule: Address phase is exactly one cycle long. A Subordinate cannot extend the address phase; it can only extend the data phase via HREADY.
ahb_fsm_hints.data_phase_rule: Manager holds write data stable throughout the extended cycles; for reads, the Subordinate does not have to provide valid HRDATA until the transfer is about to complete.
ahb_fsm_hints.pipeline_rule: Address phase of any transfer occurs DURING the data phase of the previous transfer. Extending one transfer's data phase has the side-effect of extending the address phase of the next.
ahb_fsm_hints.burst_constancy_rule: HSIZE, HBURST, HWRITE, HPROT, HMASTLOCK, HNONSEC must remain constant for all beats of a burst.
manager_per_burst_fsm: Drive first beat: HTRANS=NONSEQ + address + control signals.
If burst length > 1: drive subsequent beats with HTRANS=SEQ and incrementing/wrapping address.
If unable to continue immediately during the burst (undefined-length burst only): drive HTRANS=BUSY with the address that the next SEQ transfer will use.
On the cycle following the LAST data beat (HREADY=HIGH for the final SEQ): drive HTRANS=IDLE or start the next NONSEQ.
subordinate_per_transfer_fsm: Sample HSELx, HADDR, HBURST, HSIZE, HTRANS, HPROT, HWRITE only when HREADY=HIGH (previous transfer completing).
For HTRANS=IDLE or HTRANS=BUSY: provide zero-wait-state OKAY (HREADYOUT=HIGH, HRESP=0); transfer ignored.
For HTRANS=NONSEQ or HTRANS=SEQ: perform the access; drive HREADYOUT=LOW to insert wait states if needed.
On completion: drive HREADYOUT=HIGH with HRESP=OKAY (or ERROR — two cycles).
AHB5 Exclusive: also drive HEXOKAY in parallel with HRESP.

ahb_error_response_2cyc_fsm: Cycle 1: Subordinate drives HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=0 (signals ERROR, holds data phase).
Cycle 2: Subordinate drives HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=1 (ERROR observed by Manager).
Manager option A: continue the remaining transfers in the burst.
Manager option B: cancel the remaining transfers; must drive HTRANS=IDLE during the two-cycle ERROR response.
ahb_locked_access_fsm: Manager asserts HMASTLOCK in the same cycle as the address/control signals of the locked-sequence's first transfer.
Bus is 'locked' once HMASTLOCK=1 AND HSEL is asserted (if present) AND HREADY=HIGH for at least one cycle.
All transfers in the locked sequence must address the same Subordinate region.
Manager deasserts HMASTLOCK with the address of the FIRST unlocked transfer.
Recommendation: insert an IDLE transfer after a locked sequence.

apb_fsm_states.outputs: PSELx=1, PENABLE=0; PADDR + PWRITE + PWDATA (if write) + PSTRB + PPROT all driven by bridge
PSELx=1, PENABLE=1; Subordinate drives PREADY (and PRDATA for reads, PSLVERR if used)

apb_fsm_transitions.cond: Transfer required (bridge starts a new APB transfer)
PREADY=0 (Subordinate inserting wait states; bridge holds PADDR/PWRITE/PSELx/PENABLE/PWDATA/PSTRB/PPROT stable)
PREADY=1 AND no further transfer follows
PREADY=1 AND another transfer follows immediately

anti_deadlock_rule.ahb: No combinational path from any HREADY back to a Manager output (HSEL / HTRANS) is permitted; the Manager must drive its address-phase signals based on registered state only.
anti_deadlock_rule.apb: Bridge must not feed PREADY combinationally back into PSELx or PENABLE; bridge holds outputs stable while PREADY=LOW.

exit_from_reset.ahb: Earliest the Manager may begin a non-IDLE transfer is the first rising HCLK after HRESETn=HIGH; integrators typically initialize HTRANS=IDLE during reset.
exit_from_reset.apb: Bus enters IDLE (PSELx=0, PENABLE=0) on PRESETn=LOW.

default_ready_state_recommendation.AHB: Subordinates may default HREADYOUT=HIGH; only drive LOW to insert wait states.
default_ready_state_recommendation.APB: Subordinates that have a fixed two-cycle access may tie PREADY HIGH; PREADY can take any value while PENABLE is LOW.

transfer_type_change_during_wait_states_.IDLE_to_NONSEQ: Permitted; HTRANS must then remain constant until HREADY=HIGH.
transfer_type_change_during_wait_states_.BUSY_to_SEQ_fixed: Permitted in fixed-length bursts; HTRANS must then remain constant until HREADY=HIGH.
transfer_type_change_during_wait_states_.BUSY_to_other_undef: Permitted in undefined-length bursts (BUSY can change to any other type when HREADY=LOW).

address_change_during_wait_states_ahb.IDLE_change_once: Manager can change the address ONCE during an IDLE-waited transfer; address must then remain constant until HREADY=HIGH.
address_change_during_wait_states_ahb.after_ERROR: Manager is permitted to change the address while HREADY=LOW following a Subordinate ERROR response.

evidence.quote: A transfer consists of two phases: Address — Lasts for a single HCLK cycle unless it is extended by the previous bus transfer. Data — Might require several HCLK cycles. Use the HREADY signal to control the number of clock cycles required to complete the transfer.

Subordinates use HREADYOUT to insert wait states if they require more time to provide or sample the data. During a waited transfer, the Manager is restricted to what changes it can make to the transfer type and address.
When the Subordinate is requesting wait states, the Manager can only change the address once, except as described in: During an IDLE transfer; After an ERROR response.
The Subordinate uses HRESP to indicate the success or failure of a transfer. ... ERROR response is a two-cycle response. (Figure 5-2 shows HRESP=1, HREADY=0 then HRESP=1, HREADY=1.)
The Exclusive Access Monitor records ExclusiveID + address for an exclusive read and returns HEXOKAY for a successful exclusive write.

The state machine operates through the following states: IDLE — default state. SETUP — when a transfer is required the bus moves into the SETUP state, where the appropriate select signal PSELx is asserted. The bus only remains in the SETUP state for one clock cycle and always moves to the ACCESS state on the next rising edge of the clock. ACCESS — the enable signal PENABLE is asserted. Exit from the ACCESS state is controlled by PREADY: PREADY LOW keeps the bus in ACCESS; PREADY HIGH exits to IDLE if no more transfers, or to SETUP if another transfer follows.
